# February 2021 Texas Power Crisis Analysis

## Introduction

During February 2021, severe winter storms caused widespread power grid outages in the state of Texas. This analysis explores the impacts of the power crisis on residential areas in Houston, Texas during the winter storms.

## Load Packages

```{r}
#| output: False

library(sf)          # vector handling
library(stars)       # raster handling
library(terra)       # raster handling
library(tidyverse)
library(tmap)        # map making
library(gt)          # table formatting
```

## Prepare Data

### Load Data

```{r}
# Load February 7, 2021 VIIRS data for Houston tiles
VIIRS_feb07a <- stars::read_stars('data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021038.h08v05.001.2021039064328.tif')
VIIRS_feb07b <- stars::read_stars('data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021038.h08v06.001.2021039064329.tif')
# Combine February 7, 2021 tiles
pre_storm <- st_mosaic(VIIRS_feb07a, VIIRS_feb07b)

# Load February 16, 2021 VIIRS data for Houston tiles
VIIRS_feb16a <- stars::read_stars('data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021047.h08v05.001.2021048091106.tif')
VIIRS_feb16b <- stars::read_stars('data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021047.h08v06.001.2021048091105.tif')
# Combine February 16, 2021 tiles
blackout <- st_mosaic(VIIRS_feb16a, VIIRS_feb16b)

# Load data for Houston area houses
houses <- st_read('data/gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1.gpkg', query = "SELECT *
FROM gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1 
WHERE (type IS NULL AND name IS NULL) 
OR type in ('residential', 'apartments', 'house', 'static_caravan', 'detached')", quiet = TRUE)

# Load data for Texas highways
highways <- st_read('data/gis_osm_roads_free_1.gpkg', query = "SELECT * FROM gis_osm_roads_free_1 WHERE fclass='motorway'", quiet = TRUE)
```

### Check Coordinate Reference Systems

```{r}
# Verify that pre_storm and blackout raster CRSs match
if(st_crs(pre_storm) == st_crs(blackout)) {
  print(paste('CRS match. CRS is:', st_crs(pre_storm)))
}else{
  warning('CRS do not match')
  print(paste('pre_storm CRS is', st_crs(pre_storm)))
  print(paste('blackout CRS is', st_crs(blackout)))
}
```

```{r}
# Verify that houses and highways vector CRSs match
if(st_crs(highways) == st_crs(houses)) {
  print(paste('CRS match. CRS is:', st_crs(highways)))
}else{
  warning('CRS do not match')
  print(paste('highways CRS is', st_crs(highways)))
  print(paste('houses CRS is', st_crs(houses)))
}
```

The nighttime light data, houses data, and roads data all use the EPSG 4326 coordinate reference system.

## Visualize Blackout

To visualize the blackout, Houston-area data from NASA's Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) for two clear nights were used: February 7, 2021 (before the storms) and February 16, 2021 (during the blackout).

To exclude unrealistic values from appearing on the maps, the data were filtered to include only radiance values less than 500 nW cm-2sr-1. A time series of radiance values from Figure 3 in the paper *Anisotropic characteristic of artificial light at night - Systematic investigation with VIIRS DNB multi-temporal observations* showed that the highest radiance values for a residential area in Houston were in the 160 to 180 cm-2sr-1 range (Ma *et al.*). I used these numbers to help inform my conservative choice of realistic radiance values (\< 500 cm-2sr-1).

```{r}
# Define Houston area
houston_area <- st_bbox(c(xmin = -96.5, ymin = 29, xmax = -94.5, ymax = 30.5),
                        crs = st_crs(pre_storm))

# Crop pre storm and blackout rasters to Houston area
pre_storm_crop <- st_crop(pre_storm, houston_area)
blackout_crop <- st_crop(blackout, houston_area)

# Set unrealistic radiance values to NA (values greater than 500)
pre_storm_crop[pre_storm_crop > 500] <- NA
blackout_crop[blackout_crop > 500] <- NA

# Stack and name data layers for visualization
feb_storm_stacked <- c(pre_storm_crop, blackout_crop)
names(feb_storm_stacked) <- c("February 7, 2021 (Pre-Storm)", "February 16, 2021 (Blackout)")

```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 9
#| out-width: "100%"
#| warning: false
#| error: false

# Visualize nighttime lights from February 7, 2021 and February 16, 2021
blackout_map <- tm_shape(feb_storm_stacked) +
      tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale(values = "magma"),
                col.legend = tm_legend(title = "Light Intensity\n(nW cm⁻²sr⁻¹)",
                                       title.size = 0.7,
                                       position = tm_pos_out('right'))) +
      tm_facets(as.layers = FALSE, nrow = 2, free.scales = FALSE) +
      tm_graticules(lwd = 0.25, col = "white", alpha = 0.5, labels.size = 0.4, labels.rot = c(90, 0)) +
      tm_title("Houston, Texas Nighttime Light Radiance", 
                fontface = "bold",
                position = tm_pos_out("center", "top"))

blackout_map
```

These maps visualize nighttime lights in the Houston area before (top map) and during (bottom map) the February 2021 power crisis. Dark areas in the bottom map are dispersed throughout the Houston area, indicating that power loss was widespread.

## Identify Blackout Areas

Areas that experienced a blackout were defined as cells within the VIIRS data that experienced a drop of more than 200 nW cm-2sr-1 between February 7 and February 16, 2021.

```{r}
#| warning: false

# Calculate difference in night light intensity pre and post storm
night_difference <- pre_storm - blackout

# Convert to SpatRaster for terra operations
night_difference <- rast(night_difference)

# Classify areas that experienced drop of more than 200 nW cm-2sr-1 (blackout)
blackout_rcl <- matrix(c(-Inf, 200, NA, # no blackout
                           200, Inf, 1), # experienced blackout
                           ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE) 
blackout_areas <- classify(night_difference, rcl = blackout_rcl)
blackout_areas <- st_as_stars(blackout_areas) # convert back to stars for stars operations

# Vectorize blackout mask
blackout_mask <- blackout_areas |> 
                 st_as_sf() |> 
                 st_make_valid()

# Crop blackout mask to Houston area and reproject to EPSG:3083
houston_blackout <- st_crop(blackout_mask, houston_area) |> st_transform(crs = "EPSG:3083")
```

Highways may have experienced changes in nighttime light radiance that were unrelated to power grid failure. To refine the analysis, areas near major highways were excluded.

```{r}
#| warning: false

# Reproject highways data to EPSG:3083 (coordinate system unit of measure is meters)
highways <- st_transform(highways, crs = "EPSG:3083")

# Create 200 m buffer around highways
highway_buffer_200m <- highways |> st_union() |> st_buffer(dist = 200)

# Identify blackout areas further than 200 m from highways
houston_blackout_exclude_hwy <- st_difference(houston_blackout, highway_buffer_200m)

```

## Visualize Homes That Lost Power

Homes that experienced a drop in radiance of more than 200 nW cm-2sr-1 between February 7 and February 16, 2021 *and* were located further than 200 meters from a highway were identified as impacted by the blackout.

```{r}
#| warning: false

# Reproject houses data to EPSG:3083
houses <- st_transform(houses, crs = "EPSG:3083")

# Identify homes that experienced a blackout
blackout_houses <- st_intersection(houses, houston_blackout_exclude_hwy)

# Convert houses into points for mapping
house_points <- st_point_on_surface(houses)
blackout_house_points <- st_point_on_surface(blackout_houses)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 9
#| out-width: "100%"

# Assign colors
all_houses_color <- "#fffddc"
blackout_color <-  "#943524"

houston_blackout_homes <- tm_basemap("https://{s}.basemaps.cartocdn.com/dark_all/{z}/{x}/{y}{r}.png?key=cb1_5bb7_1_34c461c6b579795316bae83a") + # Add nighttime basemap
      tm_graticules(lwd = 0.25, col = "gray", alpha = 0.7) + # Add latitude and longitude lines
      tm_shape(house_points) + # Add houses
      tm_symbols(fill = all_houses_color, shape = 15, size = 0.05) +
      tm_shape(blackout_house_points) + # Add houses that lost power
      tm_symbols(fill = blackout_color, shape = 15, size = 0.05) +
      tm_add_legend(fill = c(all_houses_color, blackout_color), 
                    labels = c("Unimpacted", "Power Lost"), 
                    position = tm_pos_out('right')) +
      tm_title("Houston Area Residences Impacted By Power Crisis, February 16, 2021",
                fontface = "bold",
                position = tm_pos_out("center", "top"))
houston_blackout_homes
```

As shown in the map, residential power loss was not isolated to just one region of Houston. Homes in many neighborhoods throughout the city lost power during the February 2021 Texas power crisis.

## Estimate the Number of Homes That Lost Power

```{r}
power_lost_houston <- tibble(
  `Total Homes` = length(unique(houses$osm_id)), # Estimate of total homes
  `Homes that Lost Power` = length(unique(blackout_houses$osm_id)), # Estimate of impacted homes
  `Percentage of Homes that Lost Power` = paste((round(length(unique(blackout_houses$osm_id)) / length(unique(houses$osm_id)) * 100, digits = 1)), "%") # Percentage of impacted homes
)

power_lost_houston |> 
  gt() |> 
  tab_header(title = "Houston Residences Impacted By Power Crisis,\nFebruary 16, 2021")
```

Based on this analysis, an estimated 157,407 Houston residences out of 475,941 (33.1%) experienced power outages during the February 2021 storms.

## Reflections and Limitations

The February 2021 power crisis was not isolated to just one general region or neighborhood. Power loss during the storms was complex and widespread, with an estimated 33.1% of Houston area residences impacted by the blackouts. While these results are compelling, they provide only a limited snapshot of the extent of power grid failure. There were several nights during the February storms where there was too much cloud cover for satellite imagery to be useful. Analyzing power loss that occurred on additional nights beyond just February 16th would have helped provide a more accurate picture of the extent of the blackouts.
